title: Larger models: upward Löwenheim–Skolem and model sizes
summary: Build large elementary extensions, obtain models of every sufficiently large infinite size, and distinguish size changes from independence witnesses.
abstract: How much can first-order axioms determine the size of a structure? A theory with an infinite model has models of every infinite cardinality at least as large as its language. Naming distinct elements and applying compactness also gives any infinite structure arbitrarily large elementary extensions, preserving every formula about the original elements. A bound involving the original domain lets us choose an extension of exactly the desired size. These constructions produce nonisomorphic models that agree on every sentence. They therefore do not establish independence: to show that the axioms leave a sentence undecided, we need models giving opposite answers to that sentence.
